title: NEET-UG 2026 Scrapped After Paper Leak, Doctors Demand NTA Overhaul
excerpt: Supreme Court petition seeks court-supervised re-exam as 22 lakh students face uncertainty for second year running
body:
India's National Testing Agency cancelled the NEET-UG 2026 medical entrance exam on May 3 after investigators in Rajasthan discovered a handwritten guess paper matching over 60 questions from the official test. The CBI has opened a probe, and a fresh petition filed in the Supreme Court demands that the NTA be replaced entirely with a technologically advanced body capable of securing the exam process.

**A Pattern, Not an Aberration:** This is not the first time NEET has been engulfed in controversy. In 2024, 67 candidates received perfect scores under suspicious circumstances, triggering a nationwide scandal that led to arrests and CBI investigations. That crisis was supposed to be a wake-up call. Instead, the 2026 leak — involving a pre-circulated document with over 120 Chemistry questions and several Biology matches — suggests the systemic rot runs deeper than any single exam cycle.

The Federation of All India Medical Association (FAIMA) and the Health Reform Doctors Association (HRDA) have jointly condemned the breach as a complete systemic failure, calling for prosecution of what they describe as entrenched exam mafias. A separate doctors' body wrote directly to Prime Minister Modi, urging the dissolution of both the NTA and the National Medical Commission.

**What the Court Petition Seeks:** The Supreme Court filing, submitted on May 13, asks for an interim judicial committee — including a cybersecurity expert and forensic scientist — to oversee the re-examination. The petitioners argue that simply rescheduling the test under the same agency guarantees nothing. They want a permanent replacement body with end-to-end digital security, biometric authentication, and real-time monitoring.

**The Stakes for NRI Families:** For the estimated 300,000 NRI and OCI-card-holding families with children considering medical education in India, the chaos is more than abstract. NEET is the sole gateway to MBBS admissions across the country, and many diaspora families invest years of preparation and significant coaching fees banking on a fair process. Two consecutive compromised exam cycles raise fundamental questions about whether the system can be trusted.

The 22.79 lakh students who sat for the May 3 exam now face an indefinite wait for re-exam dates, with the academic calendar already compressed. Nationwide protests have erupted in Delhi, Rajasthan, and Karnataka, with opposition leaders accusing the ruling government of negligence.

**What Comes Next:** The Supreme Court is expected to hear the petition within days. If the bench orders a court-supervised re-exam, it would set a precedent for judicial oversight of national entrance tests — a move that could reshape how India conducts high-stakes examinations for years to come.
